findings.claim: A failed then retried delivery can appear failure-free.
findings.resolution: Retain listener StratumStats; emit attempt success/failure deltas; complete requires zero failures. A disposable CHECK-constraint regression recovered all eight clients after eight failures and emitted complete=false.

findings.claim: Per-listener admission/timeouts are undisclosed and configuration literals can drift.
findings.resolution: Explicit 128-permit, 30-second phase and 20-second write settings; report actual listener/Coordinator/runtime values and observed PG settings. Report discloses 128 versus 256 aggregate permits.

findings.claim: The waited generic save is not the compact-issued runtime transaction; any public error passes.
findings.resolution: Drive save_issued_job_compact with persisted original dependency under its own lock wait and assert its exact revision error. Public refusal remains an additional zero-row check because its API deliberately erases causes. Removed immutable-value tautology.

findings.claim: Delivered-row validation cannot expose committed rows that were never delivered.
findings.resolution: After successful delivery, count all issued rows per frontend and new parent, report unmatched rows and require zero; exclude old-parent login jobs and prepared records. Frozen v1 counts remain unknown.

findings.claim: Setup failure has a different and unbounded schema teardown path.
findings.resolution: Create fallible direct/node resources before the schema, construct the Fixture immediately after CREATE, and route partial setup through the same bounded close routine.

findings.claim: Disposable schema/listener scaffolding is duplicated across suites.
findings.resolution: Real maintenance overlap, but shared extraction would change compact_runtime_e2e and compact_runtime_scale outside the explicitly owned harness/report branch scope. Record as test-infrastructure follow-up on issue275; per-fixture cleanup divergence is fixed here. This is not a measured runtime correctness defect.

findings.claim: Replace four explicit gate sites and closures with a Selection/Case dispatcher.
findings.resolution: Current gate::site! calls identify each actual test at its entry point; four explicit cases are easy to audit, and typed dispatcher adds a parallel test registry and must preserve source-site identity. No wrong gate or reachable failure was found. Keep explicit required_database_url on scale.

findings.claim: Prefix-only metrics selection could later admit decreasing gauges.
findings.resolution: Restrict measurement parsing explicitly to histogram count/sum series; preserve unknown absent samples and existing finite/nonnegative delta validation.

findings.claim: The outer case timeout can erase delivery evidence after long login.
findings.resolution: Pass the absolute 240-second case deadline into delivery; cap login and delivery at the case deadline minus one second reserved for reporting. Login failures emit B275_SETUP_FAILURE; effective delivery budget is recorded. Original 30/120/240-second maxima are not increased.

findings.claim: Appending options may discard an existing URL options value (reviewer marked unverified).
findings.resolution: Checked pinned sqlx-postgres 0.8.6 src/options/parse.rs:92-98: duplicate options values are concatenated with a space in query order. Existing settings remain and appended -csearch_path takes precedence for isolation; no defect shown.

findings.claim: Client decode is serialized in one test task and affects measured latency.
findings.resolution: Report explicitly states same-process two-thread runtime, one receive task, debug profile, and serialized JSON decode inside the observed endpoint; no server-only latency or production qualification claim.

findings.claim: PG16/exact durability pin couples ordinary tests to the benchmark environment.
findings.resolution: Intentional controlled-fixture contract explicitly requested by the user. CI uses PG16; changing the qualification environment should fail visibly and require deliberate revalidation. No relaxation of versions or durability.

findings.claim: Two-second waiter observation can fail on a heavily loaded host.
findings.resolution: Explicit failure is intentional and cannot establish false performance acceptance. It preserves the existing deadline and prevents claiming controlled contention without observing the waiter; no target/deadline relaxation requested.

findings.claim: Any external same-key waiter can satisfy the contention probe.
findings.resolution: Tag all fixture pools with a unique application_name, join pg_locks to pg_stat_activity on that tag, emit waiter PID and require persistence elapsed >= the three-second hold. No other operation in the serialized fixture can wait on that key.
